content: MECR Trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase, mitochondrial, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the MECR gene. This gene consists of 15 exons. The protein product of the gene has a molecular weight of approximately 2 kDa and is composed of 189 amino acids. Mass spectrometry data has identified 10 distinct peptides derived from this protein. The mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) pathway, in which this enzyme plays a role, is critical for the synthesis of lipoic acid. Lipoic acid is an essential cofactor for several mitochondrial enzymes that are involved in aerobic metabolism. In experimental models, specifically in mice, the targeted deletion of the MecR gene in Purkinje cells results in neurodegeneration, highlighting the importance of this gene in maintaining neuronal health. Clinically, mutations in the MECR gene have been implicated in causing MECR-related progressive neurodegeneration with dystonia, optic atrophy, and basal ganglia abnormalities, also known as MEPAN syndrome. This is a neurometabolic disorder that disrupts the mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) pathway. Patients with MEPAN syndrome typically exhibit autosomal recessive mutations in the MECR gene and present with symptoms such as childhood-onset dystonia, optic atrophy, and abnormal MRI findings in the basal ganglia.
